programme: AIP, ESRRA and NR2C2 converge on ESR1 as a shared target (AIP and ESRRA additionally co-target the canonical estrogen-response gene TFF1), forming a nuclear-receptor cross-regulatory circuit that tunes estrogen-receptor-alpha-dependent transcription: AIP acts as a chaperone/co-regulator that licenses nuclear receptor maturation, ESRRA is an orphan estrogen-related receptor that binds ERE-like elements in parallel to ESR1, and NR2C2 (TR4) supplies a further ligand-independent input into the same estrogen-responsive gene set.
role_in_a: Not documented in the retrieved record — none of the three factors has an Open Targets association or a literature hit for fibromyalgia. If this circuit is active in the blood compartment these cohorts were sampled from, its expected role would be to set peripheral estrogen-responsive transcriptional tone, which is at least plausible given fibromyalgia's strong female predominance and symptom fluctuation across the menstrual cycle, but that specific link is not established by any evidence gathered here.
role_in_b: ESRRA is independently placed in ovarian cancer (percentile 0.924; PMID 33751740 ties ESRRA copy-number variation to histological grade), consistent with its general role driving oxidative and estrogen-responsive metabolic transcription in hormone-sensitive tumors. NR2C2 has direct mechanistic support (PMID 41615304: NR2C2 transcriptionally activates NAA30 to promote ovarian cancer progression). AIP itself is not placed in ovarian cancer by the retrieved record (no Open Targets association, ambiguous/off-topic papers), so its role here is inferred from its general nuclear-receptor co-regulator function rather than direct evidence.
shared_axis: Fibromyalgia cohorts are sampled from blood, the compartment that reads out systemic estrogen exposure, while ovarian tissue is the organ that produces and locally responds to that same hormone; a conserved AIP–ESRRA–NR2C2 circuit acting on ESR1 in both compartments would reflect a shared systemic estrogen-signaling module common to both conditions rather than a mechanism specific to either disease.
reasoning: The module is nameable from real biology — three concordant factors converge on ESR1 (with AIP and ESRRA also sharing TFF1), and two of the three (ESRRA, NR2C2) are independently placed in ovarian cancer by percentile and direct PMIDs — but not one factor in the whole set carries any Open Targets association or literature hit for fibromyalgia, so the cross-disease link rests on reasoning about shared, estrogen-sensitive, female-predominant physiology rather than on anything retrieved. That is enough to call the programme itself credible but not enough to call the pairing established or clinically obvious.
support: PMID 33751740 — ESRRA copy-number variation associated with ovarian cancer histological grade, placing ESRRA directly in disease B; PMID 41615304 — NR2C2 transcriptionally activates NAA30 to promote ovarian cancer progression, placing NR2C2 directly in disease B; no PMID places AIP, or any factor, in fibromyalgia.
how_to_falsify: In blood-derived PBMC or whole-blood RNA-seq from fibromyalgia cohorts (stratified by menstrual/hormonal status), test whether AIP, ESRRA and NR2C2 co-vary with ESR1-pathway activity (e.g. TFF1 expression or an ERE reporter signature); if their expression is uncorrelated with ESR1-target activity in this tissue, or if ChIP/CUT&RUN in blood or ovarian cell lines shows AIP/ESRRA/NR2C2 do not co-occupy ESR1 or TFF1 regulatory regions, the proposed shared circuit does not hold.
caveats: Only 2 independent cohort pairs underlie the 64 patient-group comparisons, so the high concordance counts reflect repeated stratification of the same two cohorts, not independent replication. RFXANK's MHC-class-II antigen-presentation targets (HLA-DR/DP/DQ/DM, CIITA), NKRF's NF-kB/oxidative-stress targets, MSX2's Wnt/BMP developmental targets, and SMARCD3's muscle-differentiation targets (MYOG, SGCA) all sit in the same concordant list but do not fit this account and are left unexplained rather than forced in. Tissue-generic master regulators (STAT1, ETS1, FOXO1/3, IRF8, BCL6) were already removed before ranking, so the account does not lean on a generic immune or stress-response driver, and single-cohort artifacts (e.g. STAT5B, GRHL2, RORA) were excluded and do not affect the module named here.
